facts.statement: The study used a rat model of spinal cord injury to test the effects of the nanoparticles.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: Researchers created nanoparticles coated with macrophage membranes that carry the drug fasudil and manganese dioxide to target inflammation.
facts.subject: other

facts.statement: The macrophage coating helped the particles avoid being eaten by immune cells and allowed them to accumulate more in the injury site in living animals.
facts.subject: other

facts.statement: Treatment with the nanoparticles lowered inflammatory activity in microglia and reduced the buildup of reactive oxygen species.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: The nanoparticles also improved the movement of blood vessel cells and their ability to form new vessels, and helped neural stem cells differentiate.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: In the injured rats, the treatment reduced the size of the lesion cavity and the amount of scar tissue (fibrosis).
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: The study found that the nanoparticles promoted neurological recovery in the injured rats.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: Gene expression analysis and protein testing showed that the treatment was associated with changes in specific inflammatory signaling pathways.
facts.subject: animals
